instrument: tidycrm test: one two-finger pinch of factor 1.1 with its midpoint 300 px right of and 200 px below centre, run through the rig's pinch arithmetic (zoomBy + panDelta) with the perspective units-per-pixel; Before: pan moves 27.3 world units against the 0.17 the wheel's corrected step moves for the same zoom; After: within 1% of the wheel's
title: A touch pinch flings tidycrm's cube out of frame (orthographic anchor)
body:
## Summary
The camera rig's pinch (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/useCameraRig.ts:452) zooms and pans tidycrm's perspective scene with the orthographic anchor arithmetic, so a 10% pinch off-centre moves the pan about 157 times too far, the wrong way on x.

## Description
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/space/useWheelZoom.ts turns the rig's wheel off (`wheel: "none"`, Blocks.tsx:98) because zoomAt's identity is exact only for an orthographic stage, and converts the anchor into perspective units itself. Its own header says the same gap breaks "the pinch and the shift-drag", and the rig's pinch is not governed by the `wheel` option: useCameraRig.ts:452 runs `zoomBy(effect.factor, effect.mid)` with the raw pixel midpoint and `panDelta` in pixels over zoom. On a touchscreen that is the only zoom gesture there is (no wheel, and +/- are keyboard). canvas-graph/viewport-transform: the anchor must be expressed in the transform's own units. Fixed looks like the header's own proposal - `CameraRigOptions.unitsPerPixel?: (pose, frame) => number`, defaulting to `1 / pose.zoom` and threaded into zoomAt and panDelta - after which tidycrm passes its `CAMERA_Z / focal` and deletes useWheelZoom; or, inside tidycrm alone, a touch handler beside useWheelZoom with the rig's pinch disabled.

## Flow
- a reader on a touch screen pinches out over the cube, midpoint off-centre
- the gesture reducer emits `pinch` with the factor and the midpoint
- useCameraRig.ts:452 calls zoomBy with the pixel midpoint: the pan is solved as if one scene unit were one pixel
- observed (probe): 1.1x at (900,600) in a 1200x800 frame moves pan to {-27.3, -18.2}; the perspective-correct step moves it to {+0.17, -0.12}; the cube is 2.6 units across

## Expected impact
Touch readers can zoom the space without losing the cube. Could break: the kit's other two rigs if the default is not exactly today's arithmetic; the kit's camera tests pin that.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a pinch zooms at the fingers instead of throwing the scene away
Before: probe, kit zoomAt with the raw midpoint: pan {-27.27, -18.18} for a 1.1x pinch; tidycrm's converted step for the same zoom at the same point: {+0.17, -0.12} (ratio 157, x mirrored)
After: not built - the fix is a kit contract (demo-kit-zoom-engine) or a touch handler of tidycrm's own
Method: probe - both arithmetics run in node on the real functions; the rig's pinch path itself needs the instrument above
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/useCameraRig.ts:452-456 case "pinch": zoomBy(effect.factor, effect.mid); panDelta(effect.pan.x, effect.pan.y, zoom)
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/Blocks.tsx:98 wheel: "none" (the pinch is not covered by it)
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/space/useWheelZoom.ts:39-42 "after which a perspective scene gets the wheel, the pinch and the shift-drag right"
probe (scratch): zoomAt(REST, 1.1, {x:900,y:600}, {w:1200,h:800}) -> pan {-27.27,-18.18}; wheelPose(...) same zoom -> pan {0.174,-0.116}; CAMERA_FOV 30, CAMERA_Z 9.5

instrument: test/space.test.ts: poseName and snapNear at each named pose shifted by -2pi and +2pi; Before: -2pi returns null and does not snap; After: the pose's label and a snap
title: After one full turn left the four named poses stop being recognised or snapped
body:
## Summary
poseName and snapNear (examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/space/camera.ts:336, :350) wrap yaw with JS `%`, which keeps the sign, so once the reader has orbited a full turn to the left no pose is named, its button is never pressed and the magnet never takes.

## Description
Yaw is free (BOUNDS.yaw "free"), so a reader who drags left past -pi keeps going negative. `((d + PI) % 2PI) - PI` is a correct wrap only for d + PI >= 0; at d = -2PI it gives -2PI and `Math.abs` reads it as a full turn away. World.tsx:148 presses a pose button by `poseName`, and Blocks.tsx:107 hands `snapNear` to the rig as its magnet. The kit already exports the correct one, `angleDelta` (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/camera.ts:84), and Blocks.tsx:175 uses it for the same comparison. Fixed: both functions use angleDelta.

## Flow
- the reader drags the cube one full turn to the left and lets go on the front view
- the magnet runs snapNear: dy = 2PI, off > SNAP_NEAR, no snap
- CameraNote runs poseName: null, so "front" is not pressed and the caption has no name
- turning back right past -PI makes both work again

## Expected impact
The camera's named poses mean the same thing after any amount of orbiting. Could break nothing inside one turn; the arithmetic is the kit's tested helper.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a named pose is recognised however many turns the reader has made
Before: probe on the real functions: yaw = front + 2PI -> "front", snaps; yaw = front - 2PI -> null, no snap (pose unchanged); front - 4PI -> null
After: not built - camera.ts belongs to tidycrm-spatial-model-tools
Method: probe - the two functions run in node at four yaws; the fix is one helper swap in another context's file
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/space/camera.ts:336 const dy = Math.abs(((pose.yaw - p.yaw + Math.PI) % (2 * Math.PI)) - Math.PI);  // snapNear
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/space/camera.ts:350 same expression  // poseName
examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/camera.ts:84 export const angleDelta = (a, b) => ...

instrument: a scene test under @react-three/test-renderer (or a browser capture): render OctantScene with cellsOf(sheet), re-render with cellsOf after normalizeFields + flagStale on BLK-05, read the instanced mesh's matrices and colours; Before: unchanged; After: the five changed dots' scales differ
title: The L0 table dots keep their first colour and size after any write
body:
## Summary
Octant (examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/l0/octants/Scene.tsx:151) writes the instanced dots' matrices and colours once, behind a `placed` ref, so after a tidy, a flag or a merge the picture keeps showing the sheet as it was first drawn.

## Description
Blocks.tsx recomputes `cells` from each new sheet the server action's revalidation hands it, and Octant re-renders with the new `cell` - but its `useFrame` only places the dots while `placed.current` is false, which it is exactly once per mount, and the octants never remount (keyed by database id). Each dot's size is the table's deviations against the worst table's and its colour is the table's strongest claim, so both move with every write. The wash is prop-driven and does update; only the imperative instance writes are stale. Fixed: key the placement on the dots' content (mark and weight per dot) instead of a boolean, and invalidate.

## Flow
- at L0, open a table, tidy its phones and flag its stale rows, close back to L0
- cellsOf(sheet) now differs for five of the 46 dots
- Octant re-renders; placed.current is true; the matrices and colours are not rewritten
- the dot of the table just cleaned keeps its old size and ink until a reload

## Expected impact
The picture an agent or a reader looks at after a write shows the write. Could break: nothing outside the placement block.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the L0 dots follow the data
Before: probe: normalizeFields + flagStale on BLK-05 changes 5 of 46 dots (mark or weight) in cellsOf; Scene.tsx's guard writes them 0 times after the first frame
After: not built - no instrument can render the three.js scene in this runner
Method: probe - the data side measured in node on the seed; the render side read, not run
Result: better
Gate: none

instrument: a DOM test (jsdom or a browser) of Dossier: open it, focus is on the card, press Shift+Tab; Before: document.activeElement is outside the dialog; After: it is the dialog's last control
title: Shift+Tab from the opened dossier leaves the modal for the sheet behind it
body:
## Summary
The dossier's Tab trap (examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/Dossier.tsx:183) wraps only from its first control, but the card itself holds focus on open, so the first Shift+Tab walks out of an `aria-modal` dialog into the sheet underneath.

## Description
Dossier.tsx:156 focuses the card (tabIndex -1) rather than the close button, deliberately. The trap then compares `document.activeElement` with the first and last focusable controls; the card is neither, so Shift+Tab is not prevented and the browser moves to the previous focusable element in document order - the dossier layer is rendered after `.bk-sheet` (Blocks.tsx:234-316), so that is the sheet's last control. Nothing behind the dialog is inert. Fixed: treat the card as "before the first" (`active === first || active === sheetRef.current` wraps to last).

## Flow
- open a table's dossier by click or by an agent's open_item; focus lands on the card
- press Shift+Tab
- onKeyDown: activeElement is the card, not `first`; no preventDefault
- focus moves to a control on the sheet behind the scrim, while the dialog says it is modal

## Expected impact
A keyboard or screen-reader reader stays inside the dossier until they close it. Could break: nothing; Tab forward is unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the modal keeps focus
Before: walked: card focused -> Shift+Tab -> no wrap branch matches (Dossier.tsx:183-189) -> default focus move out of the layer
After: one extra comparison wraps it to the last control
Method: simulation - this runner strips types without compiling JSX and tidycrm has no DOM library, so the handler cannot be run here
Result: better
Gate: none

instrument: a DOM test of Field + useProjector with a stub rig: emit a pose that puts every slab edge-on, then tab into the grid; Before: focus lands on a card with data-behind=true; After: the hidden cards are inert and focus goes to the frame or the first visible card
title: An L1 label the camera has hidden is still focusable and still read out
body:
## Summary
When the camera is edge-on, behind a slab or in flight, useProjector marks a card `data-behind="true"` and the stylesheet makes it invisible (opacity 0, no pointer events), but it keeps its tabindex and its accessible name, so the roving focus and a screen reader land on cards nobody can see.

## Description
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/field/useProjector.ts:185-187 sets `dataset.behind` and stops; examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/level0/l0.css:112 hides it by opacity, and l1-cells.css:122 does the same for the whole grid during the flight beat. Field.tsx:135 still gives the roving card tabIndex 0 and the arrows still step to the others. The focus ring is drawn on a transparent element. Fixed: `node.inert = !facing` beside the dataset write (and the grid inert while `phase === "flight"`), with the roving step skipping inert cards.

## Flow
- inside a database, orbit until the rank is edge-on (|view . face| < FACING_FLOOR)
- every label is taken out visually
- Tab into the grid: focus lands on an invisible card; arrows move between invisible cards; Enter opens a dossier from nothing visible

## Expected impact
What a keyboard or screen-reader reader can reach matches what is drawn. Could break: focus held on a card that goes inert mid-orbit moves to body; the frame should take it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - hidden labels are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree
Before: walked: facingOn false -> data-behind true -> opacity 0 only; tabIndex unchanged (Field.tsx:135)
After: inert removes them from both
Method: simulation - no DOM in this runner; the projector runs inside a React effect
Result: better
Gate: none

instrument: a DOM test of Field inside a rig-bound frame: pointerdown on a card, move 20 px, pointerup (the rig swallows the click), then Enter on the focused card; Before: onOpenTable not called; After: called once
title: The first Enter on an L1 card after a drag that began on a card is ignored
body:
## Summary
Field.tsx keeps its own drag-versus-click check (`down` ref and SLOP, examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/Field.tsx:137-145), but since the challenge run the rig swallows a drag's trailing click before it reaches the card, so `down` is never cleared and the next keyboard click - whose clientX/Y are 0 - reads as a 500 px drag and is dropped.

## Description
The rig (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/useCameraRig.ts:490, capture-phase native click listener) stops the click that follows any gesture past DRAG_SLOP (4 px). Field's onPointerDown still records the press; its onClick, which would reset it, never runs. A click synthesised by Enter or Space carries clientX = clientY = 0, so `Math.hypot(0 - x, 0 - y) > SLOP` and the handler returns. Fixed: drop Field's own slop check (the rig already owns "drag wins over click"), or ignore keyboard clicks (`event.detail === 0`).

## Flow
- at L1, press on a card and drag to orbit; let go (the rig swallows the click)
- Tab or arrow to a card and press Enter
- onClick: from = the stale press point; distance to (0,0) > 5; return
- the second Enter works, because the first cleared `down`

## Expected impact
Keyboard opening of a table is never eaten by an earlier drag. Could break: nothing; the rig's swallow already covers pointer drags.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every Enter on a card opens it
Before: walked: drag -> swallowClick (rig) -> Field.down stays set -> keyboard click at (0,0) rejected
After: no stale state to reject it
Method: simulation - needs a DOM and the rig's listener together; not runnable here
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The merge confirmation disarms after 8 s, before a reader can finish it
body:
## Summary
useArm (examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/useRun.ts:19) drops an armed merge or delete after 8 seconds, but the merge confirmation it shows is about 75 words, so the panel snaps back while a reader at an ordinary pace is still reading it.

## Description
The timeout is a deliberate safety ("a control left armed while you read something else is a control you can fire by accident"). It measures time since arming, not inattention: the reader who is reading the consequence - which now has to name the phone and activity date the merge carries over (hitl-approval/consent-gates, built in this round) - is the one it disarms. Options: restart the timer on pointer movement or focus inside the arm panel; scale it to the text; or disarm on blur/leave rather than on a clock. Each changes how long a destructive act stays one click away, which is the owner's call.

## Flow
- press "Merge the identity pair"; the confirmation appears
- read it at about 4 words a second (~19 s for 75 words)
- at 8 s the panel returns to the unarmed buttons; the reader must arm again and read faster

## Expected impact
A person can read what they are consenting to before it disappears. Could break: a longer or activity-held window keeps a destructive control live longer.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the consent stays on screen long enough to be read
Before: 8 000 ms window; merge question ~75 words (was ~47 before this round's disclosure, already ~12 s at 238 wpm)
After: depends on the chosen rule; not built
Method: probe - word count of Gate.tsx's question with seed names, timer read from useRun.ts
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen

title: tc-scales.css is mounted nowhere and reads an undeclared --tc-edge
body:
## Summary
examples/tidycrm/design/tc-scales.css declares a scale layer under `[data-variant="scale"]`, which nothing in the repo mounts; its header says the variant's shell imports it, its four elevation steps read `var(--tc-edge)`, which no file declares, and its compact density breaks the two-step rule its comment says holds.

## Description
`git grep 'data-variant="scale"' -- examples/tidycrm` finds only this file, and nothing imports it (the hirelane challenge scout reached the same verdict). Header lines 14-17 still describe an import "by the variant's own shell". Lines 106-109 build every elevation on `var(--tc-edge)`; with it undeclared the whole box-shadow value is invalid at computed time. Line 148 binds compact to steps 7/4/2/1 and says "Rule holds", but item (2) to pair (1) is one step. build-tokens.mjs, the other file of this context, marks itself RETIRED and is pinned by test/tokens.test.ts; this one is not. It cannot simply be edited at the top: examples/demo-kit/src/ui/demo-kit.css:67 cites it by line number (26-31). Options: mark it retired at the foot and pin that in tokens.test.ts, or delete it and repoint the kit's citation.

## Flow
- a reader follows demo-kit.css:12 or :67 to this file for the type floor rationale
- the header tells them a shell imports it; none does
- copying its elevation steps gives shadows that do not render

## Expected impact
The file says what it is. Could break: the line citation in demo-kit.css if lines move.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a cited design artifact states its own status and is internally consistent
Before: 0 consumers (git grep); 4 reads of an undeclared custom property; 1 density mode breaking its stated rule; header claims an import
After: depends on keep-and-mark vs delete
Method: probe - git grep for the selector and the property over the repo
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
git grep -n -e "--tc-edge": examples/tidycrm/design/tc-scales.css:106,107,108,109 only (no declaration)
git grep 'data-variant="scale"' -- examples/tidycrm: tc-scales.css:16,45,149,160 only
examples/tidycrm/design/tc-scales.css:148-153 compact: gap-item space-2, gap-pair space-1 (one step)
examples/demo-kit/src/ui/demo-kit.css:67 cites tidycrm/design/tc-scales.css:26-31
